verses.text: Word reached David that the Philistines were attacking Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing floors.
David asked the LORD, “Should I go and attack these Philistines?” The LORD answered, “Go, strike them down, and rescue Keilah.”
David's men told him, “We're afraid even here in Judah. How much worse will it be if we go to Keilah to face the Philistine army?”
David asked the LORD again. The LORD answered, “Get up and go down to Keilah. I'll hand the Philistines over to you.”
David and his men went to Keilah, fought the Philistines, and took their livestock. They struck them down in great numbers and rescued the people of Keilah.
When Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he brought an ephod with him.
When Saul heard David had gone to Keilah, he said, “God has handed him over to me. He's trapped himself by going into a town with gates and bars.”
Saul called up all the troops to go down to Keilah and besiege David and his men.
David knew Saul was plotting against him. He told Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.”
Then David prayed, “LORD, God of Israel, I've heard that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the town because of me.
Will the people of Keilah hand me over? Will Saul come down, as I've heard? LORD, God of Israel, please tell me.” The LORD answered, “He'll come down.”
David asked, “Will the people of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?” The LORD answered, “They'll hand you over.”
David and his men, about six hundred in all, left Keilah and went wherever they could. When Saul heard David had escaped, he called off the trip.
David stayed in wilderness strongholds and in the hills of the wilderness of Ziph. Saul looked for him every day, but God didn't hand David over to him.
David knew Saul had come out to kill him. At the time, David was in the woods in the wilderness of Ziph.
Jonathan son of Saul went to see David in the woods and helped him find strength in God.
He told him, “Don't be afraid. My father Saul won't get his hands on you. You'll be king over Israel, and I'll be at your side. Even my father knows that.”
The two made a covenant before the LORD. David stayed in the woods, and Jonathan went home.
Some people from Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and told him, “David is hiding in our territory, in the strongholds in the woods on the hill of Hachilah, south of the desert.
Come down whenever you're ready, King, and we'll hand him over to you.”
Saul said, “May the LORD bless you for having compassion on me.
Go and make certain where he's staying and who has seen him there. I've been told he's very clever.
Find out all the places he hides, then come back when you're sure. I'll go with you. If he's in the land, I'll search him out among all the clans of Judah.”
They set out for Ziph ahead of Saul. David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah south of the desert.
Saul and his men went looking for David. When David heard, he went down to the rock in the wilderness of Maon and stayed there. Saul heard about it and went after him.
Saul went along one side of the mountain while David and his men went along the other. David hurried to get away as Saul and his men closed in to capture them.
Then a messenger came to Saul. “Come quickly! The Philistines have raided the land!”
Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to fight the Philistines. That's why the place was called Sela Hammahlekoth.
David left that place and stayed in the strongholds of En Gedi.
